KUALA LUMPUR – A covered pedestrian walkway linking Kuala Lumpur landmarks such as Independence Square and the Central Market. More restored heritage buildings. Larger duty-free perks.
These are among the measures Malaysia is banking on to woo more tourists, as it steps up efforts to improve the visitor experience and connectivity ahead of the Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link launch.
The Visit Malaysia 2026 campaign, which started promotions in 2025, will be extended to 2027, with RM935 million (S$293 million) earmarked for tourism in the 2027 budget unveiled on Oct 9, up by 32.6% from RM705 million in 2026.
In 2025, Malaysia attracted a record 42.2 million tourists, the most among South-east Asian nations that year. While the target of 47 million tourists for 2026 has been extended to 2027, around 28.8 million tourists visited in the first eight months of 2026, with Singaporeans leading the Chinese and Indonesians in arrivals.
The government is also betting on heritage restoration to attract visitors. Drawing from the success of the restored colonial Sultan Abdul Samad Building, which Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said in his budget speech had attracted half a million local and foreign visitors since its reopening in February, the Kuala Lumpur Railway Station, the century-old KTMB Railway Administration Building and the iconic skyscraper Dayabumi Complex in KL are next to be restored.
Farther north and in eastern Malaysia, travellers are set to enjoy a higher duty-free purchase limit of RM10,000 in Langkawi and Labuan if they stay at least 48 hours, up from RM1,000 with separate one-litre limits for alcohol previously.
Johor steps up transport plans ahead of RTS launch
Beyond tourism, Malaysia is seeking to ease congestion in Johor ahead of the planned February 2027 launch of the RTS Link between Singapore and Malaysia. Better connectivity is also central to its ambitions for the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ).
Unveiling the 2027 budget on Oct 9, Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said traffic congestion in Johor must be addressed urgently. He said the Elevated Autonomous Rapid Transit (e-ART) system will be the main solution, alongside more bus routes, higher KTM Komuter train frequencies and Grab Shuttle services.
These will help with traffic dispersal and onward connections to other parts of Johor from Bukit Chagar, where the RTS Link train carrying up to 10,000 passengers an hour from Singapore’s Woodlands North will stop.
KTM Komuter trains can connect travellers arriving at JB Sentral to other parts of Johor, including tourist destinations such as Kluang and Kulai. Grab Shuttle also offers a shared-ride option from Johor Bahru’s city centre to key locations such as shopping malls and hospitals.
The e-ART could particularly benefit travellers unfamiliar with local roads, encouraging tourists to explore beyond the immediate station area, said USCI’s professor Hanafi Hamzah, a tourism management expert.
He also welcomed the plan to build 22km of covered walkways in KL linked to tourist landmarks, benefiting tourists from neighbouring Singapore and Thailand without cars.
“Walking is an attractive way to discover a city,” he told The Straits Times. “More pedestrian movement may encourage spontaneous visits to cafes, craft outlets, local restaurants and smaller attractions.”
Malaysia is also preparing its border infrastructure for greater cross-border traffic.
The allocation for the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency will rise more than 13-fold, from RM37 million in 2026 to RM490 million in 2027.
In a statement on Oct 10, the border agency said it would prioritise strengthening its officers’ competencies as it prepares for RTS Link operations to keep pace with the increased movement of people, goods and trade.
The Singapore Business Federation projects Singaporeans will spend $1.05 billion more across the Causeway.
JS-SEZ seeks to draw more investment
In his budget speech on Oct 9, Anwar also gave an update on the JS-SEZ, noting that it had recorded RM132 billion in investments from 2025 until June 2026.
The special economic zone was conceptualised in January 2025, with a 3,505 sq km area intended to promote investment and free up movement of goods and people between Johor and Singapore.
The JS-SEZ’s masterplan will be jointly launched with Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong at the end of 2026, said Anwar. Malaysia previously said that the blueprint would be released during the next Malaysia-Singapore leaders’ retreat, expected in December.
Anwar also offered new details about the Nexus Sedenak industrial hub, first mentioned by the Finance Ministry in June, saying it could draw RM12 billion in investments and create 45,000 jobs.
The budget provides for upgrades to roads leading to the 1,188ha site, redeveloped from an oil palm plantation. Anwar said a “Queen Bee approach” would be used, with an anchor investor helping to attract other businesses.
Leo Leow, the country director for Malaysia at consultancy Turner & Townsend, said the ideal Queen Bee could be a major advanced manufacturing leader, especially in semiconductors or electronics, that can attract a wider ecosystem of suppliers and technology partners.
He said improved connectivity in Johor could benefit a host of sectors, especially occupants of the JS-SEZ.
“Manufacturing, industrial and logistics operators can benefit from improved access to labour... Retail, hospitality and commercial operators can also benefit from improved accessibility for customers and employees,” he told ST.
Tax perks to attract regional and global headquarters
Anwar also noted the need to make it easier to do business in Malaysia, both through tax incentives and greater flexibility in allowing companies to bring in skilled talent.
An enhanced Global Services Hub (GSH) incentive, which offers a special 5% tax rate to new companies joining the scheme for up to 30 years, is the standout measure among the budget’s offerings for regional and global businesses, said Steve Chia, tax leader for PwC Malaysia.
Under the scheme, a company must be incorporated in Malaysia, where it runs the group's regional or global operations, according to the Malaysian Investment Development Authority. Income from qualifying GSH activities, including those in the JS-SEZ, will be taxed at 5%.
“This gives groups the long-term certainty to locate regional headquarters, shared services and treasury centres in Malaysia,” he added.

articles.title: Indonesia seeks stronger growth by protecting purchasing power - ANTARA News
articles.summary: Indonesia seeks stronger growth by protecting purchasing power  ANTARA News
articles.full_text:
File - Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs Airlangga Hartarto attends the Indonesia Economic Summit (IEC) 2026 in Jakarta on Tuesday (February 3, 2026). ANTARA/Bayu Saputra/am.
Looking ahead to 2027, the government is preparing sustainable policies designed to transform social assistance from a safety net into a driver of economic empowerment.
Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs Airlangga Hartarto has announced several stimulus programs for the fourth quarter of 2026, including 10-kilogram rice assistance for 33.24 million beneficiaries and a monthly wage subsidy of Rp300,000 (around US$16.77) for 13.3 million workers.
The government is also preparing to open bank accounts for citizens aged 17 and above, with a focus on people living in poverty and those vulnerable to it.
Together, these three initiatives signal a shift toward combining social protection with broader financial inclusion. Looking ahead to 2027, the government's economic agenda will expand further.
The purchasing power cushion provided at the end of 2026 does not stand alone; it is designed to build momentum when linked with broader initiatives spanning employment, skills training, workers' protection, taxation, and housing.
In 2027, the government plans to continue its internship program for 150,000 participants and provide vocational training for 300,000 people. Together, these programs aim to address key labor market challenges, including unemployment.
Beyond supporting people facing economic pressures, the government also needs to strengthen their ability to compete in the job market by equipping them with skills that meet industry demands.
On the income front, the government is preparing an income tax reduction for workers earning less than Rp10 million (around US$559) per month, a measure expected to benefit approximately 7.5 million people. An adjustment to the tax-free income threshold is also on the agenda.
Tax policy is therefore being considered not only as a means of generating state revenue but also as a tool to support household spending. Under this policy package, allowing workers to retain more of their income is intended to boost disposable income and stimulate consumption.
Relief also extends to the housing sector. The government is preparing to expand its government-borne Value-Added Tax (VAT) incentive for housing, alongside a subsidized mortgage program offering a fixed interest rate of 6 percent.
The 6 percent fixed-rate mortgage is intended for fixed-income earners making up to Rp17 million per month who are purchasing homes priced at up to Rp500 million.
The measure would broaden access to homeownership for middle-income buyers whose monthly earnings exceed the Rp14 million income ceiling for the 5 percent interest rate under the Housing Financing Liquidity Facility (FLPP) scheme.
For households, homeownership meets a fundamental need while providing a foundation for long-term wealth building. For the wider economy, the housing sector is a key growth driver, stimulating demand across construction, building materials, finance, labor, and related supply chains.
Workforce protection
Worker protection is also part of the government's agenda. It is planning to extend workplace injury insurance and death benefits to informal workers, alongside adjustments to job loss insurance benefits.
These measures are intended to ensure that workers do not have to bear the financial burden of losing their income alone.
Taken together, these policies signal a strategic shift from cushioning immediate consumption toward strengthening people's long-term earning capacity.
While food assistance and wage subsidies provide short-term relief, vocational training, internships, tax incentives, housing support, and social security are intended to establish a more resilient foundation for future economic growth.
This approach aligns with the growth framework outlined by Airlangga ahead of the drafting of the 2027 economic agenda.
The Indonesian government has set a target of achieving 6 percent economic growth in 2027, identifying investment, higher productivity, human capital development, and value-added exports as key prerequisites.
Under this framework, citizens are not viewed merely as passive recipients of assistance. Instead, they are positioned as active contributors to national economic growth through employment, consumption, skills development, and productivity.
Data from Statistics Indonesia (BPS) shows that the economy grew 5.29 percent year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026. Inflation stood at 3.28 percent year-on-year in September, remaining within the national target range. Meanwhile, exports reached US$193.64 billion from January through August 2026, generating a trade surplus of US$7.25 billion.
In the manufacturing sector, Indonesia's Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) returned to expansionary territory in September, reaching 52.4 after falling to 49.8 in August. The rebound provides a backdrop for the government to move beyond consumption support and focus on strengthening the production side of the economy.
Meanwhile, Bank Indonesia recorded year-on-year growth of 13.65 percent in bank lending in August 2026, driven by a 25.11 percent surge in investment loans. The expansion in investment financing aligns with government efforts to increase production capacity and capital investment.
Under the 2027 state budget, the government has earmarked Rp4,106.3 trillion in state spending and projected a budget deficit of 2.4 percent of GDP, alongside its 6 percent economic growth target.
Budget priorities include food, energy, education, healthcare, downstreaming and industrialization, infrastructure, housing, community-based economic development, and poverty reduction.
The stimulus package announced in late September forms part of a broader, long-term strategy.
The government is introducing protective measures to cushion the public against short-term pressures on purchasing power while laying the groundwork for stronger earnings, productivity, investment, and output over the longer term.
Achieving stronger growth requires better coordination among skilled workers, investing businesses, industries that generate added value, and markets capable of absorbing increased output.
Under this approach, economic support serves as a starting point rather than an end in itself. While policies introduced in late 2026 aim to safeguard households' economic stability, the 2027 agenda seeks to unlock broader economic momentum through higher productivity, stronger investment, and higher-value production.

The opposition Democrat Party has called for better access to financial assistance for flood victims in Bangkok, saying unclear and delayed relief measures have forced some affected traders to turn to loan sharks to keep their businesses afloat.
Korn Chatikavanij, the party’s deputy leader and a party-list MP, made the call during a visit to Klong Chan housing estate in Bangkok on Saturday to hear residents’ concerns and assess flood damage.
More than 10,000 people live in the estate, where flooding persisted for over a week from Sept 26. The disaster damaged vehicles and equipment used to earn a living, as well as almost all of the more than 400 shops in the area, Mr Korn said.
Floodwaters exceeding 1.5 metres damaged shop fittings, electrical appliances, refrigeration equipment and stock. An optical shop, for example, lost most of its eye-testing equipment and merchandise, worth hundreds of thousands of baht.
Mr Korn said the biggest loss was not property but the ability to earn a living. Many residents could not resume normal life, while some insured vehicle owners faced losses because insurance payouts might not cover the full cost of repairs or replacement.
He said government relief remained unclear in terms of the amount, timing and scope of assistance.
Although the Government Savings Bank (GSB) had publicised emergency loans, complicated eligibility requirements, including transaction records, commercial registration and credit bureau restrictions, had prevented many affected traders from accessing the funds.
The party proposed four urgent measures: setting up relief registration centres in affected neighbourhoods, particularly heavily flooded areas; waiving shop rents charged by the National Housing Authority for at least two weeks; requiring the Office of the Insurance Commission to ensure prompt claims payments and prevent insurers from shifting losses onto policyholders; and easing access to emergency loans.
Under the proposal, Mr Korn said, the GSB should increase the emergency loan ceiling for flood-hit business operators to 200,000 baht, with no interest for six months, followed by an annual interest rate of no more than 7%, and a repayment period of at least two years.
He said eligibility rules should be relaxed, approvals expedited and paperwork reduced.

Two deep-water container terminals in the Cai Mep-Thi Vai area have launched a shared berth system expected to increase their combined handling capacity by up to 900,000 TEUs a year, as Ho Chi Minh City seeks to strengthen its position as a regional shipping and logistics hub.
Cai Mep International Terminal Co. (CMIT) and Tan Cang-Cai Mep Thi Vai Terminal Co. (TCTT) began commercial operations at their joint berth on Friday, linking their adjacent facilities to form a continuous 1,200-meter quay.
The shared berth connects the quay areas of the two terminals, allowing them to coordinate the use of berthing space, equipment and personnel to serve vessels more efficiently.
The two terminals have similar quay elevations, aligned berth edges, and crane rail systems that can be connected, enabling more flexible operations across the combined facility.
Under the new operating model, the shared berth can accommodate three large vessels simultaneously, compared with a maximum of two previously.
The arrangement is expected to increase operating capacity at each terminal by around 30-40%, equivalent to an additional 400,000-500,000 TEUs annually. Across both terminals, the system could provide nearly 900,000 TEUs of additional annual capacity.
The expanded capacity is expected to improve the terminals’ ability to handle large container ships and respond to growing demand for deep-water port services.

| Mr. Shantanu Chakraborty, Country Director of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) in Vietnam | 
 How does the ADB assess Vietnam's economic situation from the beginning of 2026 to the present? What factors will shape growth in the coming period, sir?
 Since the beginning of the year, Vietnam's economic outlook has been very positive and has had a ripple effect across many sectors. The economy has entered a period of solid growth, supported by manufacturing, services, foreign direct investment (FDI), public investment, exports, and domestic demand.
 In its September update to the Asian Development Outlook, the ADB raised its growth forecast for Vietnam to 7.8% in 2026 and 7.6% in 2027, reflecting better-than-expected results in the first half of 2026.
 Growth in the 2026-2027 period will be shaped by several factors, including accelerated disbursement of public investment, sustained production resilience, continued FDI inflows, and the recovery of the service sector and domestic consumption supporting growth. Continued institutional reforms and improvements to the business environment will also play a crucial role in sustaining private investment.
 However, risks remain. As a highly open economy, Vietnam is vulnerable to changes in external demand, uncertainty in trade policy, energy price volatility, exchange rate pressures, and tighter global financial conditions. Domestically, rapid credit growth, reliance on imports, and inflationary pressures need to be closely monitored. 
|  | 
| The Vietnamese economy is assessed by international experts as developing steadily. (In the photo: Exports at Chan May Port (Chan May - Lang Co Economic Zone). Photo: Le Toan) | 
 According to him, what risks, both domestic and external, should Vietnam pay particular attention to in order to maintain its growth momentum?
 Key external risks include weakening global demand, uncertainty in trade policy, tariffs and non-tariff barriers, geopolitical tensions, rising energy prices, supply chain disruptions, and exchange rate pressures. These risks can impact Vietnam through exports, imported inputs, logistics costs, investment flows, financial markets, and business confidence. Given Vietnam's deep integration into global trade and production networks, external shocks can quickly put pressure on production, exports, and FDI.
 Domestic risks also require close policy attention. Growth heavily reliant on investment, especially if overly dependent on bank credit, can exacerbate vulnerabilities in the financial sector. The ADB notes that rapid credit expansion coupled with investment-driven growth can increase financial risks, while small businesses continue to struggle to access capital.
 Other risks include inflationary pressures, exchange rate volatility, concerns about asset quality, exposure to the real estate sector, and the possibility of increased imports that may not quickly translate into improvements in productivity, output, or export growth. Therefore, the main challenge is to sustain strong growth while ensuring macroeconomic stability, credit quality, and domestic production capacity.
 So, how should fiscal and monetary policies be balanced to support growth while maintaining macroeconomic and financial stability, sir?
 Vietnam should maintain a balanced and appropriately adjusted policy framework. Monetary policy needs to remain flexible but prudent, ensuring adequate liquidity for production sectors, while closely monitoring inflationary pressures, exchange rates, credit quality, and risks in asset markets.
 In the current environment, widespread monetary easing could increase risks to inflation, exchange rates, and financial stability. The issue lies not only in the rate of credit growth, but also in where that credit is allocated and whether it helps to boost productivity and debt repayment capacity.
 Fiscal policy can play a larger role, but the focus should be on quality, not just scale. Public investment needs to be accelerated in areas with high economic spillover effects, including transport, logistics, energy, power grids, digital infrastructure, climate change adaptation, skills, and health . These investments can support aggregate demand in the short term while strengthening productivity and competitiveness in the medium term.
 The most effective approach is to reduce over-reliance on monetary policy by using fiscal policy and structural reforms to expand the supply capacity of the economy. High, sustainable growth needs to be supported by better infrastructure, stronger institutions, more robust private investment, and more developed capital markets.
 How can Vietnam better leverage different types of investment to boost productivity, innovation, and growth?
 In my opinion, Vietnam can utilize investment capital more effectively by shifting the focus from the volume of capital mobilized to improvements in productivity and the value that capital creates. Public investment should not only be evaluated by the disbursement rate, but also based on its contribution to reducing logistics costs, improving the reliability of energy supply, expanding regional connectivity, supporting digital transformation , enhancing resilience to climate change, and creating incentives to attract private investment.
 Foreign direct investment (FDI) continues to play a crucial role in Vietnam's growth, exports, technology transfer, and employment. However, in the next phase, greater emphasis should be placed on investment quality, increasing domestic value, technology diffusion, skills development, domestic procurement, and strengthening linkages with domestic businesses. Vietnam needs to shift from simply attracting foreign-invested projects to building dynamic ecosystems around FDI areas, creating conditions for domestic businesses to develop alongside multinational corporations.
 Domestic private investment is equally important. Vietnamese businesses need better access to land, long-term capital, technology, skilled labor, data, markets, and international standards. By using public investment to reduce costs, FDI to bring technology and market access, and targeted reforms to strengthen the competitiveness of domestic businesses, Vietnam can move towards a growth model increasingly based on productivity, innovation, and resilience.
 Sir, what reforms will help improve the speed and quality of public investment disbursement, attract private investment, and strengthen linkages between domestic businesses and multinational corporations?
 There are three key reform groups.
 Firstly, it is necessary to strengthen the public investment process through better project preparation, expedited approval, clarification of land clearance and bidding procedures, enhanced coordination between agencies and localities, and increased transparency in implementation.
 While accelerating disbursement is important, the quality of spending is equally crucial. Public investment should prioritize projects that reduce costs for businesses, connect production centers with markets, improve the reliability of energy and logistics systems, and create opportunities for private investment.
 Secondly, Vietnam needs to enhance favorable conditions to attract private investment. Investors need predictable policies, simplified administrative procedures, access to land and infrastructure, a stable power supply, transparent regulations, and reliable public-private partnership frameworks. Public investment should help reduce risks and costs for private investors, rather than stifle private investment.
 Third, targeted support measures are needed to strengthen linkages between domestic businesses and multinational corporations. Domestic suppliers often face limitations related to technology, quality standards, management capabilities, access to finance, certification, and reliability in delivery.
 Vietnam can address these gaps through supplier development programs, technical consulting services, skills training, quality certification, supply chain finance, and incentives related to domestic procurement and technology transfer. Stronger linkages will help increase domestic value and enable Vietnamese businesses to move up to higher value-added stages in the value chain.

articles.title: 8 Vietnamese USD Billionaires: From Ambitious Declarations to Pillars of the Private Economy - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: 8 Vietnamese USD Billionaires: From Ambitious Declarations to Pillars of the Private Economy  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
Billion-dollar assets and the ambition to take the corporation global.
 Behind Vietnam's economic rise over the past decade lies the legacy of entrepreneurs who dared to pursue goals far beyond the limits of the domestic market. Many of their initial pronouncements were met with skepticism, but over time, they have become guiding principles for building large-scale corporations.
 In 2014, billionaire Pham Nhat Vuong shared his desire for Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City's streets to be as bustling as those of Hong Kong (China) or Singapore , while emphasizing the importance of leaving a legacy for future generations.
 Over the past decade, Vingroup and Vinhomes have developed numerous large urban areas such as Vinhomes Riverside, Ocean Park, Smart City, and Grand Park, integrating housing with amenities, commerce, and services.
 Besides real estate, Mr. Pham Nhat Vuong expanded his operations into the automotive manufacturing sector. At the groundbreaking ceremony for the VinFast complex in Hai Phong in 2017, he stated his goal of bringing Vietnamese car brands to the international market.
 VinFast subsequently shifted to electric vehicle production, expanding its operations overseas and investing in manufacturing facilities in India and Indonesia . This process still presents many challenges regarding competition and business efficiency. 
 Vietnam already has some high-class urban areas.
 For billionaire Nguyen Thi Phuong Thao, the philosophy behind building Vietjet also began with a goal that went beyond simply selling airline tickets: bringing the opportunity to fly to millions of people who had never been on an airplane before.
 Vietjet commenced commercial operations in 2011, contributing to the popularization of the low-cost airline model in Vietnam. The airline expanded its domestic and international route network, developed its fleet, and built its brand beyond the domestic market. From an idea that once faced considerable skepticism, low-cost airlines have become an important part of the Vietnamese air transport market.
 In the heavy industry sector, Hoa Phat Chairman Tran Dinh Long once affirmed: "Hoa Phat will do things that others cannot do." The group has persistently invested in the steel industry, developing large-scale production complexes in Dung Quat and rising to the leading position in the domestic construction steel market.
 The preparation for producing rail steel for large-scale railway projects shows that Hoa Phat is seeking to move into segments with higher technical requirements and added value, instead of focusing solely on traditional steel products.
 In the consumer sector, billionaire Nguyen Dang Quang once aspired to have at least one Masan product in every Vietnamese family's kitchen. With its food and spice brands and retail system, Masan has built a widespread presence in consumer life. This is an example of how a private enterprise can develop from essential products into a large-scale consumer ecosystem.
 Meanwhile, billionaires Ho Hung Anh and Ngo Chi Dung respectively built Techcombank and VPBank into significant private banks, playing important roles in providing capital, financial services, and digital transformation in the banking industry.
 Eight USD billionaires, including Mr. Pham Nhat Vuong, Ms. Nguyen Thi Phuong Thao, Ms. Pham Thu Huong (Mr. Vuong's wife), Ms. Pham Thuy Hang (Mr. Vuong's sister-in-law), Mr. Tran Dinh Long, Mr. Ho Hung Anh, Mr. Ngo Chi Dung, and Mr. Nguyen Dang Quang, operate in various fields, from real estate, industry, aviation to banking, consumer goods, and technology.
 As of October 11, 2026, Mr. Pham Nhat Vuong had a net worth of $35.2 billion, ranking 66th in the world and the richest person in Vietnam. Ms. Pham Thu Huong had a net worth of $4 billion, ranking 1,067th in the world; Ms. Pham Thuy Hang had a net worth of $2.8 billion.
 Along with personal assets, the businesses associated with these entrepreneurs have also expanded in scale. By the end of June 2026, Vingroup's total assets reached over 1.3 trillion VND, Hoa Phat's nearly 279,000 billion VND, and Techcombank's nearly 1.3 trillion VND.
 Accumulated resources provide the foundation for businesses to pursue larger goals. In this context, controversial statements also partly reflect the strategic direction and risk tolerance of the leaders.
 Aspiration to reach global standards.
 However, success in the Vietnamese market does not necessarily equate to global competitiveness. In terms of revenue scale, technology, productivity, international brand recognition, and position in the value chain, most Vietnamese private corporations still lag significantly behind leading corporations in Asia and the world.
 VinFast is pursuing fierce competition in the electric vehicle industry, where Chinese, American, South Korean, and European companies possess advantages in scale, technology, supply chains, and manufacturing experience. Hoa Phat has a strong domestic position and has expanded exports, but to become a globally influential steel industry hub, the company still needs to improve its technological capabilities, product quality, and ability to participate in high-value supply chains.
 In the technology sector, FPT has progressed from software outsourcing to technology services, digital transformation, artificial intelligence (AI), and initial activities in the semiconductor field. However, Vietnamese businesses still lack a commensurate position on the world map in core technologies such as advanced chip design, large-scale semiconductor manufacturing, or the development of leading AI platforms.
 This is both the challenge and the opportunity for the next decade.
 AI, cloud computing, semiconductors, advanced materials, green energy, and robotics are reshaping the global economy. These fields require significant capital investment, highly skilled human resources, long-term research capabilities, and a robust industrial ecosystem. Not all businesses are capable of participating, but corporations that have accumulated substantial resources have a distinct advantage in expanding into these new areas.
 Vingroup is expanding its focus and investment into industry, energy, batteries, and robotics technology. FPT is pursuing AI, semiconductors, and digital infrastructure. Hoa Phat is seeking to upgrade its steel production capacity. Private banks are accelerating digitalization and developing data-driven financial services, while Masan has the opportunity to apply technology to optimize its supply chain and retail operations.
 But large capital and ambition alone are not enough to guarantee success. The technology race requires businesses to choose the right areas where they have an advantage, invest disciplinedly, build research teams, protect cash flow, and persistently pursue long-term efficiency. Expanding into new industries needs to be accompanied by genuine capabilities, rather than just chasing attention-grabbing trends.
 The role of the State is also crucial. Policies for developing science and technology, training human resources, protecting intellectual property rights, building infrastructure, and creating a level playing field can help businesses reduce costs and increase their capacity for innovation. The coordination between private resources and public policies will determine the ability to form corporations capable of competing internationally.
 South Korea's experience shows that large corporations can become the driving force of industrialization, but their strength only truly contributes in the long term when linked to productivity, exports, technological innovation, and the development of a domestic network of supporting businesses.
 For Vietnam, the expectation is not simply about the emergence of more USD billionaires or large-capitalization corporations. More importantly, it is about these businesses being able to create technology products owned and developed by Vietnamese people, increasing domestic added value, creating high-quality jobs, and helping Vietnamese businesses participate more deeply in the global supply chain.
 The ambitious, even questionable, statements of entrepreneurs can be the starting point for great journeys.
 But the ultimate measure is not the founder's net worth, but the company's international competitiveness and the sustainable value it creates for society.
 Vietnam already has businesses large enough to nurture aspirations for greater achievements. The road ahead is to transform accumulated resources into technological capabilities, ambitions into globally competitive products, and the success of a few corporations into a driving force for prosperity for the general population.

articles.title: Prospects For A Political Solution To The Myanmar Crisis – OpEd - Eurasia Review
articles.summary: Prospects For A Political Solution To The Myanmar Crisis – OpEd  Eurasia Review
articles.full_text:
Key Takeaways:
- Min Aung Hlaing’s 100-day peace initiative was rejected by major resistance groups, while his visits to India, China, Russia and selected ASEAN states aim to ease isolation, secure arms and economic support, and gain legitimacy despite ongoing air strikes and civilian casualties.
- In Rakhine, military blockades and Arakan Army operations have created shortages and disrupted trade with Bangladesh, yet limited border commerce offers relief and could revive roughly $260 million in annual exchanges if formalized under stable conditions.
- Diplomatic and military advantages will not end the conflict without a negotiated political settlement; resistance unity could block further offensives, while compromise would improve prospects for peace, Rohingya returns and regional connectivity.
A peaceful resolution to Myanmar’s prolonged conflict remains uncertain. Despite repression, displacement, economic hardship, and immense sacrifice, peace has not returned. The popular struggle against military rule has continued for more than five years, demonstrating the resilience of the resistance. The authorities continue to confront armed resistance groups without making meaningful progress toward compromise or a political settlement. The peace and stability promised after the elections have yet to materialize. Even amid the civil war, the authorities have sought to improve relations with neighboring countries, expand diplomatic engagement, enhance international acceptance, and strengthen the economy. Peace and stability in Myanmar, particularly in Rakhine State, are essential to resolving the Rohingya crisis. If the government can combine its international initiatives with credible measures to restore domestic peace, relations between Bangladesh and Myanmar could improve, supporting regional development and security.
The United Nations’ independent investigative mechanism has reported a continuing rise in the number and severity of serious crimes in Myanmar, alongside intensified military air strikes against civilians. Military forces have reportedly struck homes, schools, hospitals, religious buildings, and shelters for displaced people. Human rights organizations say violence against civilians continues in areas controlled by resistance groups through air strikes, arson, and forced displacement. Both the military and the ethnic armed group Arakan Army have been accused of widespread and systematic abuses against the Rohingya minority. Illicit economic activities, including illegal mining, drug production, human trafficking, and scam centers, help finance the conflict and deepen the human rights crisis.
After assuming the presidency, Min Aung Hlaing announced a 100-day initiative and called for peace talks with armed resistance groups. Major resistance organizations, including the Kachin Independence Organization, the Karen National Union, the Chin National Front, and the Arakan Army, rejected the proposal. Despite maintaining regular contact with the military, the Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army (MNDAA) did not participate in the 100-day peace initiative. Under pressure from China, the MNDAA is now engaged in talks with the Myanmar authorities. Because the group controls important border trade routes with China, the government, with Beijing’s support, is seeking greater influence over these routes.
If the main armed resistance groups agree to separate ceasefires, their combined effect could alter the balance of the conflict. The Myanmar military could then reposition its forces and launch new offensives, potentially prolonging the war. Critics therefore argue that the government’s 100-day peace initiative is primarily a political strategy designed to strengthen regional and international acceptance of the new electoral system.
Since taking office as president, Min Aung Hlaing has visited India, China, Russia, and several ASEAN countries. His visit to India appeared intended to reduce Myanmar’s heavy dependence on China by strengthening ties with another major regional power. During the visit, Myanmar pledged that its territory would not be used to threaten India’s security. Both sides emphasized the need to advance stalled connectivity projects, including the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project and the India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway, and set a bilateral trade target of US$5 billion.
The main subjects of Min Aung Hlaing’s visit to Russia were military cooperation, nuclear energy, space, digital technology, special economic zones, and energy projects. Relations between Russia and Myanmar now extend across defense, nuclear energy, infrastructure, and other strategic sectors. The multibillion-dollar arms trade remains central to the relationship. Diplomatically, the visit was intended to strengthen the government’s international legitimacy and strategic position through ties with a key ally, despite continued Western sanctions and isolation.
Although ASEAN has declined to formally recognize Myanmar’s military rule and continues to exclude the country from high-level meetings, Min Aung Hlaing’s recent visits have helped improve bilateral ties with individual member states. The Myanmar authorities have exploited divisions within ASEAN by cultivating relations with each member separately as part of a broader effort to break their international isolation. Official receptions in Laos, Thailand, Vietnam, and Cambodia have helped advance these ties. Analysts argue that such bilateral engagements give the military government an appearance of diplomatic influence and legitimacy, weakening ASEAN’s joint peace framework, the Five-Point Consensus. Min Aung Hlaing also urged the Thai prime minister to stop support and arms supplies from reaching Myanmar’s resistance forces.
At the same time, Myanmar and Thailand discussed border security measures to counter the smuggling of drugs and prohibited chemicals. Bangkok’s decision to restore ties amid allegations of widespread atrocities and war crimes against civilians has drawn strong criticism from Thai politicians and international human rights organizations.
During his visit to Belarus, Min Aung Hlaing held talks aimed at attracting investment. He argued that Belarusian businesses operating in Myanmar could gain access to ASEAN and the wider Asian market, while Myanmar’s exports could reach the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) through Belarus, creating reciprocal opportunities. The Myanmar authorities have long sought EAEU observer status and have held extensive discussions with EAEU representatives on cooperation in energy, agriculture, education, and transport.
The Myanmar military has maintained a prolonged blockade of roads and waterways connecting Rakhine State with the rest of the country. As a result, many civilians in Rakhine face shortages of medicine and other basic necessities. Communities have therefore sought food, medicine, fuel, and essential goods from Bangladesh and India. Military operations, the activities of the Arakan Army, restrictions on movement, and widespread insecurity have largely halted cross-border trade and made humanitarian access increasingly difficult, disrupting local livelihoods. Conditions improved somewhat when limited trade resumed along the Teknaf-Kanyin Chaung border route during the conflict. Border trade therefore serves both economic and humanitarian needs. Much of it is conducted through informal arrangements; a stable and formal framework could expand trade and strengthen economic relations between the two countries.
Before the conflict in Rakhine disrupted regional commerce, official statistics placed the annual trade volume along the Bangladesh-Rakhine border at approximately US$260 million, demonstrating the economic complementarity of the two neighboring regions. Agriculture, fisheries, marine products, livestock, forestry, and small-scale industries once formed the backbone of local livelihoods. Revitalizing these sectors could support a two-way trading relationship that benefits people on both sides of the border. Greater market access for local entrepreneurs would encourage investment and create jobs in border communities. A normalization of conditions in Rakhine would also improve the prospects for addressing the wider crisis between Bangladesh and Myanmar.
The Bangladesh-Rakhine border could become more than a simple crossing point. Realizing its potential will depend on sustained stability, investment in infrastructure, simpler trade rules, and durable cross-border cooperation. With expanding regional connectivity through the route linking Paletwa in Myanmar to Mizoram in India, the area could emerge as an important economic corridor in the Bay of Bengal region. The challenge for the Government of Bangladesh and the authorities in Rakhine is to ensure that border trade supports a more prosperous, connected, and peaceful frontier and contributes to lasting peace between the two countries.
The Myanmar authorities have yet to take effective steps to end the internal conflict. Experience over recent decades suggests that the crisis will remain difficult to resolve without a political settlement. The government is currently seeking greater international acceptance through diplomacy while maintaining its military capabilities and expanding trade and economic relations. It is also deepening ties with neighboring countries, particularly China and Russia. Myanmar has encouraged investors by emphasizing its access to wider markets and the strategic importance of its geographic position, presenting these factors as opportunities for increased investment and trade.
These initiatives are unlikely to succeed unless peace returns to the country. It remains unclear whether pressure on the resistance groups can produce a compromise. If the groups remain united and coordinate their actions, the government’s strategy may fail. If their unity fractures, however, the military could regroup and attack them separate

articles.summary: Indonesia seeks bigger role in Asia-Pacific retail industry  ANTARA News

Tangerang, Banten (ANTARA) - The Indonesian Retailers Association (Aprindo) highlighted that within the Asia-Pacific retail landscape, Indonesia is not just a massive consumer market but also a growth platform, a hub for business ecosystems, and a prominent regional player.
Aprindo Chairman Solihin said in Tangerang, Banten, on Sunday, the wholesale and retail trade industry accounted for 13.2 percent of Indonesia’s GDP in 2025, making it the third-largest contributor after manufacturing.
The sector recorded a year-on-year growth of 6.1 percent, outpacing the country's overall economic growth.
This strength is backed by the country’s population of more than 270 million with diverse consumer profiles, across urban and rural areas, where both modern and traditional retail play equally crucial roles in meeting people’s daily needs.
Nevertheless, Aprindo views Indonesia’s potential as extending beyond its domestic market.
“As a market, Indonesia offers a massive consumer base, expanding organized retail, and a steadily growing digital payment and omnichannel ecosystem," Solihin said in a statement.
As a platform, he added, Indonesia should seamlessly connect consumers, brands, micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), supply chains, and technology.
At the same time, he noted that Indonesian retailers, as regional players, are beginning to expand their capabilities beyond the domestic market.
As an example of this expansion, he pointed to Alfamart, an Aprindo member, which has entered the Philippines. This progress demonstrates that the capabilities built by Indonesia’s retail industry have real potential to scale across the regional market.
These capabilities extend beyond store formats to include management expertise, supply chain strength, brand and product value, and skilled retail human capital.
“We are also opening up opportunities for regional retail players to enter and grow in the domestic market,” he said.
This perspective demonstrates that cross-market relationships in the Asia-Pacific do not have to end in competition. The exchange of capabilities, adaptation of business models, and cross-border partnerships can unlock shared growth opportunities.
For Aprindo, the next agenda is strengthening the ecosystem that allows these opportunities to thrive, through government-industry collaboration, predictable regulations, supply chain resilience, fair digital competition, and deeper integration of MSMEs.
"Indonesia offers more than just sales opportunities. Indonesia also provides room to build partnerships and develop retail capabilities that can contribute to the growth of the Asia-Pacific region," Solihin said.

articles.title: Nghe An achieves a breakthrough in budget revenue: Driven by production and management innovation. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: Nghe An achieves a breakthrough in budget revenue: Driven by production and management innovation.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
In the first nine months of 2026, state budget revenue in Nghe An province reached over 25,700 billion VND, equivalent to 110.2% of the annual forecast, an increase of 28.2% compared to the same period last year. This result marks the recovery and growth of production and business, and also demonstrates the effectiveness of innovations in tax management, combating tax evasion, and exploiting revenue sources.
Production and business activities create momentum for increased revenue.
In 2026, amidst ongoing economic challenges, Nghe An province continued to implement solutions to promote growth, improve the investment and business environment, and support businesses in recovering production. These positive economic developments contributed to expanding budget revenue, enabling the province to achieve its annual state budget revenue target within just nine months.
By the end of August 2026, total budget revenue in the area reached 23,364 billion VND. In September, revenue continued to increase, bringing the cumulative total to over 25,700 billion VND, exceeding the annual forecast by 10.2% and increasing by 28.2% compared to the same period last year. This is a remarkable result in the context of the budget revenue collection task, which requires both ensuring resources for development and creating conditions for businesses to maintain operations and expand production.
This result has helped Nghe An rise to the top group of localities nationwide, having completed the entire statutory budget assigned by the Central Government after only two-thirds of the year.
A closer look at the revenue structure reveals that the business sector continues to play a crucial role, accounting for over 50% of total domestic revenue according to the provided data. This reflects the contribution of production and business activities to budget revenue, and also shows that maintaining the growth momentum of businesses is directly significant to the local government's ability to generate financial resources.
The growth in revenue is clearly evident in the industrial sector. In the first nine months of 2026, the industrial production index (IIP) for the entire sector is estimated to have increased by 21.49% compared to the same period last year. In the third quarter alone, the manufacturing industry recorded an IIP increase of 28.68%, with revenue reaching VND 48,860 billion.
Alongside traditional manufacturing sectors, the electronics industry continues to emerge as a notable growth driver. The commissioning of numerous projects, the expansion of production scale, and the increase in capacity have contributed to enhancing the province's industrial production capacity. Projects such as Luxvisions Innovation, Innovation Precision, Sunny Automotive, and Luxshare create further opportunities for the development of processing, manufacturing, and supporting industries.
Notably, revenue from the electronics and computer manufacturing industry in the third quarter reached VND 25,874.6 billion, 5.45 times higher than the same period last year. This result is linked to the expansion of production of high value-added goods, including camera components and products serving the electronics industry.
The development of factories is not only reflected in the scale of production but also in job creation, boosting demand for services, transportation, logistics, and supporting industries. When production is maintained stably, businesses are able to expand their markets, increase revenue, and contribute more to the local budget.
Mr. Hoang Van Lam, CEO of Minh Anh Electronics Company in Dien Thang Industrial Park, said that as a company manufacturing and processing automotive electrical equipment for a South Korean partner, the company has invested in a factory, installed production lines, and actively recruited local workers. Stable production operations create jobs and contribute to the province's revenue.
In the beer production sector, investment in equipment, cost reduction, and market expansion continue to contribute to maintaining production volume and revenue. Mr. Dang Viet Cuong, Head of Administration at Saigon - Song Lam Beer Joint Stock Company, stated that the company produced 66.7 million liters of beer in the first nine months of 2026. This achievement is linked to efforts to improve production efficiency, reduce costs, and seek new markets.
According to compiled data, the top 10 businesses and units contributing to the state budget in the area collectively contributed a total of VND 3,362.4 billion in the first nine months of the year. Leading the way is Saigon Beer - Song Lam Joint Stock Company with VND 833.99 billion; followed by Road Management Area II with VND 513.55 billion. TH Dairy Food Joint Stock Company contributed VND 309.36 billion; Saigon Beer - Nghe Tinh Joint Stock Company contributed VND 298.61 billion; Military Petrochemical Branch - MIPEC contributed VND 293.49 billion; and Bac A Commercial Joint Stock Bank contributed VND 292.45 billion.
The next companies include VSIP Nghe An Co., Ltd. with VND 251.91 billion; Petrolimex Nghe An Co., Ltd. with VND 209.17 billion; Eurowindow Sport City Real Estate Investment and Development Co., Ltd. with VND 183.54 billion; and Vietnam-Laos Economic Cooperation Corporation with VND 176.3 billion.

Along with electronics and beverages, many other industries maintained production, sought orders, and expanded their markets. Third-quarter revenues for some sectors, such as rubber, plastics, and chemicals, increased by 2 to more than 4 times compared to the same period last year. The industrial production index in September increased by 20.48%.
Several key industrial products achieved significant production volumes in the first nine months, including electronic components at 395.3 million units, fish sauce at 170.5 million liters, quarried construction stone at over 5.8 million cubic meters, and various types of beer at 108.9 million liters. Meanwhile, the garment, wood processing, and packaging industries continued to adjust their product structure, control inventory, and scale of production to adapt to market demands.
The above results show that industrial production is making a significant contribution to economic growth and budget revenue. However, to maintain the momentum of revenue growth, it is necessary to continue improving the quality of growth, developing high value-added industries, and supporting businesses in expanding their markets and improving operational efficiency.
Reforming tax administration and exploiting revenue sources.
Besides economic growth, reforming tax management methods is also one of the important solutions contributing to improving the efficiency of budget revenue collection.
In recent times, the Nghe An Tax Department has been actively promoting administrative procedure reforms, applying information technology, and digital transformation in tax management. The implementation of electronic invoices generated from cash registers, enhanced data connectivity for gasoline sales, and management of e-commerce activities have provided tax authorities with additional tools to monitor revenue, cross-reference data, and identify irregularities.
Furthermore, the management approach is gradually shifting from widespread inspections to focused risk analysis, selecting sectors and business groups with potential risks of revenue loss for thematic inspections. Targets include businesses reporting losses for many years but still expanding production, units with low profit margins, businesses in the beauty and healthcare services sector, restaurants, petroleum, and businesses with related-party transactions.
Data mining for tax management not only helps detect signs of incomplete declarations but also enhances transparency and fairness in fulfilling financial obligations among business organizations and individuals. This also provides a basis for the tax sector to use management resources more effectively, focusing on high-risk areas with significant revenue potential.
Alongside strengthening management, the tax sector implements policies on tax and land rent exemptions, reductions, and extensions as stipulated by the National Assembly and the Government. These support policies contribute to reducing cash flow pressure, creating favorable conditions for businesses to maintain operations, invest in technological innovation, and expand production. In the long term, harmonizing taxpayer support with combating tax evasion is crucial for building a stable revenue source.
Mr. Nguyen Bang Thang, Head of the Provincial Tax Department, stated that in the coming period, the Tax Department will continue to coordinate with relevant units to support businesses in stabilizing production and business operations, thereby creating additional revenue for the budget. At the same time, the department will focus on improving the efficiency of tax management for e-commerce, digital platform businesses, logistics supply chains, and land-related sectors; promote the application of big data in risk analysis; strengthen efforts to collect tax debts; and coordinate inter-agency efforts in carrying out tasks.
According to Mr. Thang, the requirement is to both strictly manage revenue sources and create a fair, transparent, and favorable business environment. The tax authorities continue to identify businesses and taxpayers as the target of service, proactively addressing difficulties and reducing compliance costs in the process of fulfilling tax obligations.
Expanding the scope for budget revenue collection in the period 2026-2030
The revenue collection results for the first nine months of the year have created more room for Nghe An to implement socio-economic development tasks. However, to maintain the revenue growth rate in the following years, the province needs to continue consolidating existing revenue sources while effectively exploiting new growth drivers.

KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — Bursa Malaysia is expected to trade within the 1,600-1,630 points range next week, with a cautious upside bias on selective accumulation of blue chips.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said valuations were becoming more attractive, although fragile investor sentiment could temper buying interest.
“Looking ahead to next week, we expect selective bargain hunting to support a gradual recovery, although geopolitical uncertainties, elevated energy prices and volatile bond yields could limit the upside,” he told Bernama.
For the trading week ended yesterday, Bursa Malaysia traded mostly higher supported by improved investor sentiment and ended the week higher, buoyed by market optimism and sustained buying activity following the Budget 2027 announcement, which provided fresh catalysts for the market.
Under Budget 2027, the federal government has allocated a total of RM459.8 billion, up 3.6 per cent from the revised 2026 allocation, equivalent to 19.8 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP).
Operating expenditure accounts for RM376.8 billion, while RM83 billion has been allocated for development expenditure (DE).
Education receives the largest allocation at almost RM69 billion, followed by health at RM47.7 billion and security with RM44 billion allocation.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that Khazanah Nasional Bhd and InvestPenang will establish a RM100 million Strategic Investment Fund to support semiconductor and advanced manufacturing companies in their early stages of growth.

“Sustaining this growth will depend on the strength of private consumption and investment, the fiscal multiplier of public spending, and the extent to which public investment crowds in private capital.
“The key policy challenge is to maximise domestic value added and growth multipliers while containing the fiscal deficit and preserving fiscal space,” he said.
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB IB) said investment growth in 2027 will be supported by higher DE of RM83 billion against RM81 billion in 2026, with major allocations directed towards transportation, education and training, healthcare, and trade and industry.

RHB IB also said the services sector should remain a key growth contributor, supported by resilient private consumption, higher tourist arrivals following Visit Malaysia 2026-2027 and initiatives to accelerate digital-economy development.
“We remain broadly optimistic about manufacturing growth, underpinned by continued expansion in export-oriented industries, healthy investment spending and business-friendly policies.
“However, external uncertainties, including the sustainability of the artificial intelligence investment cycle, geopolitical tensions and developments in United States tariff policy, could affect export demand and investment decisions.
“Malaysia’s diversified economic base and supportive domestic policies should provide some buffer against these headwinds,” it said.

articles.title: With the explosion of digital payments, banks face new risks. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: With the explosion of digital payments, banks face new risks.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
Scams are becoming increasingly sophisticated.
 Recently, five major banks in South Korea were hit by cyberattacks, resulting in the leakage of data from tens of thousands of customers. Shinhan Bank, in particular, was targeted by hackers, suspected to have used AI, causing the information of 25,000 customers to be compromised. A number of other banks, including Hana Bank, KB Kookmin Bank, Woori Bank, and Nonghyup Bank, were also targeted by similar attacks.
 Following the incident, South Korean financial regulators summoned leaders from all sectors including banking, securities, insurance, digital assets, and fintech, and instructed the entire industry to maintain the highest level of vigilance and review all information security systems.
 The story in South Korea once again raises an alarm for global banking systems in the fight against cybercrime, including Vietnam. 
|  | 
| Digital payments are becoming increasingly popular, raising concerns about cybercriminals attacking banking systems. | 
 “Security, safety, and privacy are not just issues for Vietnam, but global concerns. The need to ensure safety becomes even more crucial as payments shift strongly towards the digital environment. Besides the benefits of speed and convenience, the increase in high-tech fraud can also affect user confidence, especially among groups with limited digital skills,” said Ms. Nguyen Thi Thu, Deputy Director of the Payment Department, State Bank of Vietnam (SBV).
 In recent years, cashless payments have experienced phenomenal growth in Vietnam, consistently reaching 30-40% per year for many years. Currently, the percentage of adults with bank accounts has reached approximately 89%, and the value of cashless payments is equivalent to 28 times the GDP. However, along with the growth of cashless payments, cybercrime has also become increasingly sophisticated and complex.
 According to data from the Ministry of Public Security , in 2025, the estimated losses from online fraud in Vietnam exceeded 8 trillion VND. Associate Professor Dr. Le Thanh Tam, from the Institute of Banking and Finance (National Economics University), believes that this is only the tip of the iceberg, as only 32% of victims report to authorities, meaning the actual losses could be many times greater than the officially reported figures.
 Similarly, figures released by the State Bank of Vietnam at the end of 2025 indicate that there were 592,000 accounts and e-wallets suspected of fraud. This demonstrates the significant market risk in a context where many people still lack awareness. According to a survey by the Institute of Banking and Finance, approximately 41% of respondents had only rudimentary financial knowledge or no knowledge at all in this field.
 Experts believe that the rapid development of digital technology , coupled with the fact that people's financial management knowledge and skills have not kept pace, makes the issue of security and safety even more worrying.
 Lieutenant Colonel Nguyen Minh Duc, Deputy Director of the National Population Data Center (under C06 - Ministry of Public Security), shared that the tactics of cybercriminals are not much different from traditional criminals, only the methods have changed to cyberspace. In August and September alone, the Ministry of Public Security directed very decisively the prevention and control of cybercrime, dismantling and arresting a series of online fraudsters.
 According to a representative from C06, one of the main online scams today is impersonating judicial agencies (police, courts), calling people and providing fake links to steal their personal information. In some localities, perpetrators even impersonate officials to meet people in person, take photos of their citizen ID cards, give them small amounts of money (100-200 thousand VND), and then collect the ID card images and information to open fraudulent accounts. In addition, many perpetrators also use online recruitment scams, impersonate delivery drivers, scam people out of affection, and solicit investments…
 Shift from passive defense to proactive risk management.
 Deputy Governor of the State Bank of Vietnam, Pham Tien Dung, expressed concern that high-tech criminals are constantly changing their methods and tactics, while the rapid development of technology also poses new risks to cybersecurity and financial fraud. Currently, the State Bank of Vietnam is closely coordinating with the Ministry of Public Security to prevent, detect, and handle fraudulent activities by high-tech criminals in the payment sector.
 In recent times, thanks to data cleaning efforts, banking crimes in Vietnam have decreased significantly. Data from the Information Technology Department (State Bank of Vietnam) shows that, as of the end of September 2026, the entire industry had nearly 175 million individual customer records and nearly 3 million institutional customer records whose information (including biometrics) had been cross-referenced with the National Population Database.
 The Payment Fraud Management Information System (SIMO) also plays a significant role in risk warning.
 Currently, 147 credit institutions and payment intermediaries are connected and sharing data; the service for inquiring about accounts suspected of fraud has been implemented at 16 banks and 5 payment intermediaries. As of September 21, 2026, the service has alerted more than 5.4 million customers, of which more than 1.8 million have had transactions temporarily suspended or canceled, totaling over 6 trillion VND.
 Nevertheless, the risk of being attacked remains ever-present for both banks and customers, especially as AI continues to develop.
 Mr. Nguyen Thanh Son, Director of the Training Center (Vietnam Banking Association - VNBA), pointed out that, in the context of strong digital transformation , financial and banking fraud is becoming one of the urgent issues, requiring coordination among many entities in the financial ecosystem.
 “Digital transformation opens up many opportunities, but at the same time brings new risks. Fraud is an inseparable issue in the development of digital banking and digital payments. Notably, the rapid development of AI is making cyberattack methods increasingly sophisticated and unpredictable,” Mr. Son commented.
 One of the dangers facing banks is that financial fraud is shifting from isolated incidents to organized networks that exploit data, technology, and user behavior to attack vulnerabilities throughout the entire transaction chain.
 This necessitates a fundamental change in how banks perceive and manage risk: not just verifying customers, checking transactions, or handling incidents after they occur, but looking throughout the entire process to identify anomalies from the very beginning of a risk's formation.
 Dita Mustika, Pre-Sales Consultant for Asia Pacific at BPC, commented that fraud in digital payments is shifting from isolated incidents to organized networks, combining identity spoofing, psychological manipulation, multi-platform money transfers, and increasingly leveraging AI and deepfakes. As identity verification is strengthened, criminals tend to exploit transaction behavior, devices, and users.
 Faced with sophisticated fraud networks, experts suggest that banks need to shift from detecting unusual transactions to identifying the entire chain of behavior and connections behind them. In a real-time transaction environment, the time between an anomaly and a lost sum of money can be measured in seconds.
 Therefore, fraud prevention capabilities are no longer measured by how many layers of protection a bank has, but by its ability to see risks early enough, understand those risks correctly, and act quickly enough to prevent damage before it occurs. This is the shift from passive defense to proactive risk management in digital banking.
 Over the past period, the Ministry of Public Security and the State Bank of Vietnam have coordinated to clean up personal customer data. In 2025, the number of fraud cases decreased by 52% compared to 2024. Currently, C06 is continuing to clean up mobile subscriber data to prevent the use of unregistered SIM cards and junk SIM cards in fraudulent activities and other violations of the law . To date, more than 147 million mobile subscriber records have been cleaned and synchronized with the National Population Database. On the VNeID application, people can report fraudulent bank accounts, fraudulent phone numbers, fraudulent activities, as well as links and websites showing signs of fraud. From June to now, the State Bank of Vietnam has frozen and blocked more than 400 accounts showing signs of fraud based on this coordinated data sharing. - Mr. Nguyen Minh Duc, Deputy Director of the National Population Data Center (Department of Administrative Management of Social Order - C06, Ministry of Public Security)

articles.full_text:
President Donald Trump said Saturday it was time for Ukraine to get a new president, suggesting Volodymyr Zelenskyy has not done enough to end his country's war with Russia and blaming him for high diesel prices in the U.S.
"I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal because he could have made many deals and for some reason he never does," Trump said.
The president, who on Friday struck a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to buy diesel from Russia to address high fuel prices ahead of the U.S. midterm elections, has urged Zelenskyy for weeks to stop strikes on Russian energy infrastructure. He has also sought to blame record U.S. diesel prices on Ukraine rather than the U.S.-led war in Iran, which has elevated world energy prices.
"He wants to make problems for the world. He wants to make problems for our farmers, our ranchers, with diesel fuel," Trump said, before departing for Tennessee, where he was set to rally Republican voters.
Ukrainian and European officials on Saturday reacted to Trump's diesel deal with dismay, saying it will help pay for Russia's war efforts. Diesel prices have skyrocketed due to a collision of events, including the difficulty of getting oil out of the Middle East since the start of the Iran war, which has raised the price of all oil products.
An Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research poll conducted last month and published Oct. 1 found that Americans disapprove of Trump's handling of Iran, and blame him for higher prices.
Trump also suggested that if he had been U.S. president in 2022, "that war would have never started. There was no reason that war with Ukraine and Russia started. It started due to incompetence."
Zelenskyy has "lost 30% of your country and you've had over a million people go between the two of them, over 2 million people killed. That's a war that should have never started. And I think it's time for Ukraine to get a new president," Trump said.
Independent estimates are that about 20% of Ukraine's territory is under Russian control. British defense officials recently estimated that about half a million Russian soldiers have been killed in the war; there are no reliable recent estimates about how many Ukrainians have died.
Trump's extraordinary intervention came after Russian strikes killed at least 20 people in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, Ukrainian officials said Saturday.
Three children were among those killed when Russian aerial bombs hit residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine's State Emergency Service said Saturday. At least 18 people were wounded.
Russia and Ukraine are locked in a long-range aerial war while their armies remain largely deadlocked on the front line, more than 4 1/2 years since Moscow's full-scale invasion. Ukraine is struggling to counter escalating Russian bombardments that have killed more than 60 people over the past four days.
"Today, Russia expressed its thanks for the lifting of sanctions on diesel exports by dropping five glide bombs on residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia," Zelenskyy wrote Saturday on X.
He said every additional billion dollars Russia earns from exports would help pay for weapons components, drone upgrades, missile production and the recruitment of mercenaries, and that Moscow would only be ready to stop when its ability to fight diminished.
Zelenskyy said Ukraine was coordinating steps to counter the extra revenue Russia will receive, and that he had spoken to French President Emmanuel Macron about shoring up air defenses, warning of an increased risk of further missile strikes in the coming days.
Trump announced Friday that Russia will immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel, followed by an additional 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons "immediately thereafter." Russia will deliver an additional 3 million tons "within a short period of time" after that, he wrote.
In Kyiv, people gathered at a memorial to fallen soldiers on Independence Square greeted the deal with a mix of anger and resignation.
"Trump has once again shown his true face," said Oleksandr Petrenko, 26. "He didn't care about the situation, the shelling or the destruction of our homes. All he's interested in is oil or the fuel prices and how much Americans have to pay."
For Oksana Yakunina, a financial adviser from Kropyvnytskyi's central district, the announcement "didn't really come as a surprise."
"Trump has been working with Putin for a long time," she told The Associated Press.
Ukraine's European allies also expressed dismay at the deal and said they stood by their commitment to sanctions.
Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson said Stockholm regretted the agreement, "as energy revenues are central to the Russian war chest," and noted that the European Union would adopt its most comprehensive sanctions package yet on Monday, with 1,600 listings targeting Russia's military-industrial complex.
The German government "remains committed to the sanctions imposed on Russia and is working with its European partners on further sanctions," spokesperson Stefan Kornelius said, adding that support for Ukraine "remains unwavering."
Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski questioned whether Russia could deliver at all. Citing his embassy's reports of fuel shortages even in Moscow, and "serious sources" saying Ukraine has damaged about half of Russia's refining capacity, he asked on X: "So where will the surpluses for export come from?"
Trump's announcement was in stark contrast to a sweeping Russia sanctions law he signed last month that aimed at clamping down on the oil and gas revenues that fuel Russia's war against Ukraine.
Trump announced the deal after his envoy, Steve Witkoff, and son-in-law, Jared Kushner, met with Ukrainian officials in Miami on Friday to discuss a proposal to end the war.
Speaking about Friday's announcement, a senior Ukrainian official told AP that Ukraine was not aware of the deal before it was announced.
The official, who spoke on condition of anonymity because he was not authorized to discuss the issue publicly, said on Saturday the diesel deal announcement was not tied to anything being discussed in Florida.
He confirmed the Ukrainian delegation had left Florida and was on its way back to Ukraine.
